LAREDO, Texas — With early voting underway and nearly 14,000 Webb County ballots already cast as of Oct. 22, Laredo’s five mayoral candidates are spelling out what they would do first if elected — and four of them laid out their opening moves to KGNS this week.

Incumbent Mayor Dr. Victor Treviño put public health for young people at the top of his list, arguing that making sure Laredo’s youth have access to medical services is an investment in the city’s future citizens, according to KGNS.

District 8 Councilwoman Alyssa Cigarroa framed her first 100 days around unity: sitting down with every council member to understand each district’s needs and goals, then building a shared vision for the city from there.

Customs broker J.D. Gonzalez focused on the economy and infrastructure — keeping business-growth momentum going, reviewing the city’s water system master plan, tackling water pressure problems, and speeding up the permitting process.

Former council member Alfonso “Poncho” Casso named water as his number-one priority: protecting the river and finding alternative sources. His short-term idea is drilling on public-school land so the revenue flows back to students; his long-term vision is what he calls a Gulf water triangle.

Candidate Jorge Garza did not respond to KGNS’s request for comment, the station reported.

Five names are on the ballot for mayor, and voters have until Oct. 30 to cast an early ballot — or they can wait for Election Day, Nov. 3.

Sources: KGNS reporting (Oct. 22, 2026).

Webb Watch 956
excerpt: Four of Laredo's five mayoral candidates told KGNS their first-100-days plans: Treviño on youth health, Cigarroa on council unity, Gonzalez on business and water, Casso on new water sources. Garza didn't respond.
title: Laredo mayoral candidates outline their first-100-days plans
